resources.string: Locks the apps you choose behind your fingerprint, face, or screen lock

BioKey uses this service to see which app is on screen, so it can cover apps you\'ve chosen to lock until you authenticate. When you tap something on the home screen, in its search or in Recents, it reads its label, so a locked app is covered before it opens. While Recents is open and a locked app is unlocked, it reads the app names on the Recents cards, so closing that app there locks it again. It reads the title of each new window, to tell Google Password Manager\'s screens from sign-in sheets over other apps. It can press Home or Back for you to leave a locked app you didn\'t unlock, lock the screen when you ask after too many failed attempts, and open a locked app\'s picture-in-picture window full screen so it can be covered.\n\nBioKey does not read what you type, does not record the screen, and has no internet access. Nothing it observes leaves your device, unless you share BioKey\'s diagnostic log.

You can turn this off at any time in Android settings. To bring hidden notifications back, switch off “Hide notification content” in BioKey\'s settings first: revoking notification access instead can leave them hidden for up to a day.

A log of its own lock decisions about your locked apps, pauses, and security activity as it\'s recorded, on this phone for 3 days, at most 500 entries (after a restart with no network time, the last 500 until it\'s back). You can turn it off in Settings

Security activity: times app locking was off (BioKey\'s storage being cleared included), faces or fingerprints added or removed, notification access switched off while Hide notification content was on (and whether BioKey had it), changes made from BioKey opened with your screen lock, or within a day of a face or fingerprint change or a reset (naming the app or profile changed), reminders stopped within that day, the diagnostic log shared from such a session, the times a face or fingerprint couldn\'t be used so the screen lock was allowed, and, if you turn them on, failed unlocks. Each until you\'ve seen it (a face or fingerprint change or a reset, at least a day), then 7 days; at most 50 failed unlocks and 20 other records once seen
